recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If implementers need more detail on deriving or validating package jurisdiction from ImplementationGuide.jurisdiction, handle it in IG Publisher or package registry documentation rather than in core FHIR source.
issue_request: FHIR-28342 was a Published, Persuasive FHIR-I change request to add a jurisdiction property to FHIR NPM package.json metadata using ISO code systems, with IG package jurisdiction expected to align with the ImplementationGuide jurisdiction.
initial_application: The Jira comment records application to the Confluence NPM Package Specification in June 2021. No core source commit explicitly names FHIR-28342, but c9186a64e1 later added source/packages.html with the jurisdiction property and an ISO 3166 example, and f9a44787c4 updated the jurisdiction ValueSet link.
additional_context: source/packages.html is build-scoped via source/hierarchy.xml and linked from ImplementationGuide notes. The Confluence package page now points readers to the core packages page while retaining historical package manifest mapping text. Later FHIR-31583, already represented on the combined branch, decided that package/IG jurisdiction warning and matching behavior is publisher-discretion guidance rather than a core specification rule.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the active package page already defines optional package.json jurisdiction with {system}#{code} syntax from the Jurisdiction ValueSet and shows the ISO form in the US Core example. Adding stricter IG Publisher matching prose would go beyond the current core application and conflict with the later FHIR-31583 scope decision.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied/Persuasive with Modification package-jurisdiction documentation issue; already audited on the combined branch as no-change for core because the matching behavior is publisher discretion.
